A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoliReward research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and six pages of supplementary material. All 16 pages were compared; no material gaps prevent assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation-agreement measurements, reward-model evaluations, ablations, and video-generation post-training results in Section 4 and supplementary Sections 7 and 9.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results from v1, including annotation agreement, reward-model accuracy, post-training evaluations, and supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The binary annotation pipeline, cross-prompt pairing, BT-WT objective, and HPQA architecture remain unchanged. Section 3 and Equations (1)–(6) describe the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 250k in-house videos, 50k OOD videos, and physical-plausibility, subject-deformity, and semantic-alignment tasks. Main-text and supplementary evaluation coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains VideoScore, VideoScore-v1.1, LiFT, VisionReward, VideoPhy, UnifiedReward, and VideoAlign. The architectural, loss-function, pairing-strategy, and post-training comparator sets are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 1's caption changes the reported annotator count from three to five. Section 4.1 already states five annotators in both versions, so this resolves inconsistent protocol reporting without establishing a rerun or an actual increase in participants. Other experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The architecture and BCE ablations, reward-distribution analyses, pairing and model-scaling studies, BT/BTT/BT-WT comparison, and qualitative examples are retained unchanged, including supplementary Sections 7, 9, and 11.

E5.justification: The agreement statistics and their reporting remain unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the annotator-count caption correction does not introduce a new statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: All numerical outcomes and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains agreement rates of 77.33% and 54.67%, and Table 2 retains SoliReward's physical-plausibility/deformity accuracies of 78.48 ID and 80.08 OOD. Supplementary results and visual examples are identical.

T1.justification: The preference assumptions, BT and BT-WT formulations, and HPQA equations are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and claims about annotation noise, reward hacking, HPQA, and downstream performance. The changed resource-release statement concerns availability rather than scientific scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning reward regularization, score clustering, reward margins, and model scaling remain unchanged. The T2V validation limitation and supplementary discussion of dimension-dependent win-tie suitability are also retained.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the promise that code and benchmark will become publicly available with a statement that they are available and supplies the lian700/SoliReward GitHub address. This improves documented access information; repository contents were not assessed. Implementation details in Section 10 and Tables 11–12 are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to earlier annotation methods, reward architectures, and alignment approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to the abstract's resource-availability sentence, the Table 1 annotator count, and the arXiv version/date stamp. There is no substantive paragraph rewriting or section reorganization.

P2.justification: The added repository address causes limited text reflow across pages 1–4, and Table 1's caption changes from three to five annotators. Figures and table structures remain unchanged; pages 6–16 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects Table 1's contradiction with Section 4.1 about the number of annotators and provides a concrete code-and-benchmark access address. These are limited improvements to reporting consistency and resource discoverability. The scientific methods, evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
